```{r}
# APA-friendly p-value formatting.
# Moved here (from the later model-helpers chunk) because attribute_model_table,
# which appears earlier in the document, calls fmt_p() before that chunk runs.
fmt_p = function(p) {
  if (is.na(p)) return("")
  if (p < .001) return("< .001")
  formatC(p, digits = 3, format = "f")
}

style_table = function(kbl, footnote_text = NULL, header_above = NULL) {
  if (knitr::is_html_output()) {
    kbl = kableExtra::kable_styling(kbl, full_width = FALSE,
                                     bootstrap_options = "condensed")
    if (!is.null(header_above)) {
      kbl = kableExtra::add_header_above(kbl, header_above)
    }
    if (!is.null(footnote_text)) {
      kbl = kableExtra::footnote(kbl, general = footnote_text,
                                  general_title = "Note.",
                                  footnote_as_chunk = TRUE)
    }
    kbl
  } else {
    if (!is.null(footnote_text)) {
      cat(paste0("\n\n*Note.* ", footnote_text, "\n\n"))
    }
    kbl
  }
}
```

###LOAD DATA

```{r data-load}
library(here)
data_path = here::here("Diss_full.csv")
diss.full =  read.csv(data_path)
```

####LET'S START CLEANING

```{r}
#make all the columns lowercase to help with coding 
names(diss.full) = tolower(names(diss.full))
names(diss.full) =  iconv(names(diss.full), from = "", to = "UTF-8", sub = "")
names(diss.full) =  gsub("consent.*", "consent", names(diss.full))

```

Okay data is loaded. Now, we will clean it by the guidelines of the
pre-reg.

Participants will be excluded if they: 1) do not consent or 2) complete
the study in less than seven minutes or 3) exhibit no variability in
their responses (e.g., selecting all 5s or all 3s) across all Integrity
and likeability items, and 4) fail to complete the Integrity and
likeability ratings for at least one vignettes.

An attention check will be used to assess whether participants paid
attention during the experiment by requiring participants to select a
specific response to the question (i.e., “Select the option “somewhat
disagree” if you are paying attention.”). We will do an exploratory
analysis to determine test if excluding those who fail the attention
impacts the data.

```{r}
# Initial data count
initial_count =  nrow(diss.full)
print(initial_count)

# Clean recordeddate
diss.full$recordeddate =  str_squish(as.character(diss.full$recordeddate))
diss.full$created_date = mdy_hm(diss.full$recordeddate)

# Filters by cutoff date
cutoff_date =  as.Date("2026-01-27")
filtered_by_date = diss.full %>%
  filter(!is.na(created_date) & created_date >= cutoff_date)

count_by_date =  nrow(filtered_by_date)
print(count_by_date)

# Filter by consent
filtered_by_consent = filtered_by_date %>%
  filter(consent == "Yes, I consent")

count_by_consent =  nrow(filtered_by_consent)

# Filter by duration (exclude under 420 seconds)
filtered_by_duration = filtered_by_consent %>%
  filter(!is.na(duration..in.seconds.) & duration..in.seconds. >= 420)

count_by_duration = nrow(filtered_by_duration)

# Exclude participants under 18
filtered_by_age = filtered_by_duration %>%
  filter(is.na(age) | age >= 18)

count_by_age = nrow(filtered_by_age)


# Exclude no-variability: participants who gave identical responses across
# all Integrity and likeability items — uses apply() to avoid rowwise() issues
Integrity_like_cols = c("khon","ksin","keth","klike","kapp",
                    "shon","ssin","seth","slike","sapp",
                    "hhon","hsin","heth","hlike","happ",
                    "fhon","fsin","feth","flike","fapp",
                    "xhon","xsin","xeth","xlike","xapp",
                    "yhon","ysin","yeth","ylike","yapp")

tl_matrix = filtered_by_age %>%
  select(all_of(Integrity_like_cols)) %>%
  mutate(across(everything(), as.numeric))

has_variability = apply(tl_matrix, 1, function(row) n_distinct(na.omit(row)) > 1)
filtered_by_variability = filtered_by_age[has_variability, ]
count_by_variability = nrow(filtered_by_variability)

# Exclude attention check failures (attention1 == 2 is correct response)
filtered_by_attention = filtered_by_variability %>%
  filter(attention1 == 2)
count_by_attention = nrow(filtered_by_attention)
# Final count
final_count = nrow(filtered_by_age)

# Summary table
count_summary = data.frame(
  Step = c(
    "Initial",
    "After Date Filter",
    "After Consent Filter",
    "After Duration Filter",
    "After Age Filter",
    "Final"
  ),
  Count = c(
    initial_count,
    count_by_date,
    count_by_consent,
    count_by_duration,
    count_by_age,
    final_count
  )
)

print(count_summary)

# Print counts
cat("Total rows in diss.full:", initial_count, "\n")
cat("Rows after filtering by date:", count_by_date, "\n")
cat("Rows after filtering by consent:", count_by_consent, "\n")
cat("Rows after filtering by duration:", count_by_duration, "\n")
cat("Rows after excluding participants under 18:", count_by_age, "\n")
cat("Final rows:", final_count, "\n")
```

###Attribute 
```{r}

# Pivot the dataset

attr_long = attr_dat %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -responseid,
    names_to = "raw_item",
    values_to = "choice_raw"
  )


# Find the correct columns to attribute to the variables

attr_long = attr_long %>%
  mutate(
    severity = case_when(
      str_detect(raw_item, "^min") ~ "minor",
      str_detect(raw_item, "^mod") ~ "moderate",
      str_detect(raw_item, "^maj") ~ "major",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),
    attribute = case_when(
      str_detect(raw_item, "smart$") ~ "smarter",
      str_detect(raw_item, "bett(er)?$|bet$") ~ "better_researcher",
      str_detect(raw_item, "creat(ive)?$") ~ "creative",
      str_detect(raw_item, "rath(er)?$") ~ "rather_be",
      str_detect(raw_item, "shou(ld)?$") ~ "should_be",
      str_detect(raw_item, "reg(ard)?$") ~ "celebrated",
      str_detect(raw_item, "typ$") ~ "typical",
      str_detect(raw_item, "keep$") ~ "job_security",
      str_detect(raw_item, "get$") ~ "job_outcome",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  )


# Check to make sure it looks correct and get a count

head(attr_long, 20)
table(attr_long$severity, useNA = "ifany")
table(attr_long$attribute, useNA = "ifany")


# Set roles

attr_long2 = attr_long %>%
  tidyr::crossing(
    researcher = c("investigator", "inspector")
  )


# Figure out how many rows for the data

head(attr_long2, 20)
dim(attr_long)
dim(attr_long2)


# Find the correct columns and attribute them to role type

attr_long2 = attr_long2 %>%
  mutate(
    chosen = case_when(
      str_detect(choice_raw, "^reported researcher") &
        researcher == "investigator" ~ 1,
      str_detect(choice_raw, "^reporting researcher") &
        researcher == "inspector" ~ 1,
      str_detect(choice_raw, "^neither") ~ 0,
      TRUE ~ 0
    )
  )


# Check to make sure it looks correct and get a count

head(attr_long2, 20)
table(attr_long2$chosen, useNA = "ifany")
table(attr_long2$researcher, attr_long2$chosen)


# Set up the data for the models

attr_model_dat = attr_long2 %>%
  mutate(
    researcher_ec = if_else(
      researcher == "inspector",
      1,
      -1
    ),
    severity_num = case_when(
      severity == "minor" ~ 0,
      severity == "moderate" ~ 1,
      severity == "major" ~ 2
    ),
    responseid = factor(responseid),
    researcher = factor(
      researcher,
      levels = c("investigator", "inspector")
    ),
    severity = factor(
      severity,
      levels = c("minor", "moderate", "major")
    ),
    attribute = factor(
      attribute,
      levels = c(
        "smarter",
        "better_researcher",
        "creative",
        "rather_be",
        "should_be",
        "celebrated",
        "typical",
        "job_security",
        "job_outcome"
      )
    ),
    vignette_id = factor(severity)
  )


# Create some model tables

str(attr_model_dat)
table(attr_model_dat$researcher)
table(attr_model_dat$severity)
table(attr_model_dat$attribute, useNA = "ifany")
table(attr_model_dat$researcher_ec)
table(attr_model_dat$severity_num)

```


```{r}
# Set attribute comparisons to the grand mean rather than using
# one attribute as the reference category

contrasts(attr_model_dat$attribute) <- contr.sum(
  nlevels(attr_model_dat$attribute)
)

# Check the contrasts

contrasts(attr_model_dat$attribute)

```

```{r}

# Run our first model in the model building for the exploratory analysis

A1 = glmer(
  chosen ~ researcher_ec + attribute +
    (1 | responseid) + (1 | vignette_id),
  data = attr_model_dat,
  family = binomial,
  control = glmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa")
)


# A2 tests whether choice differs by severity, controlling for attribute

A2 = glmer(
  chosen ~ attribute + severity_num +
    (1 | responseid) + (1 | vignette_id),
  data = attr_model_dat,
  family = binomial,
  control = glmerControl(
    optimizer = "bobyqa",
    optCtrl = list(maxfun = 2e5)
  )
)


# A3 tests whether choice differs by BOTH researcher and severity,
# while controlling for attribute

A3 = glmer(
  chosen ~ researcher_ec + attribute + severity_num +
    (1 | responseid) + (1 | vignette_id),
  data = attr_model_dat,
  family = binomial,
  control = glmerControl(
    optimizer = "bobyqa",
    optCtrl = list(maxfun = 2e5)
  )
)


# A4 tests whether the effect of researcher depends on severity,
# while controlling for attribute

A4 = glmer(
  chosen ~ researcher_ec * severity_num + attribute +
    (1 | responseid) + (1 | vignette_id),
  data = attr_model_dat,
  family = binomial,
  control = glmerControl(
    optimizer = "bobyqa",
    optCtrl = list(maxfun = 2e5)
  )
)


# Summarize models

summary(A1)
summary(A2)
summary(A3)
summary(A4)

```
```{r}

model_comparisons = anova(
  A1,
  A2,
  A3,
  A4,
  test = "Chisq"
)

# Create model table

attribute_model_table = data.frame(
  Model = c(
    "A1",
    "A2",
    "A3",
    "A4"
  ),

  Predictors = c(
    "Researcher + Attribute",
    "Attribute + QRP Severity",
    "Researcher + Attribute + QRP Severity",
    "Researcher × QRP Severity + Attribute"
  ),

  AIC = c(
    AIC(A1),
    AIC(A2),
    AIC(A3),
    AIC(A4)
  ),

  BIC = c(
    BIC(A1),
    BIC(A2),
    BIC(A3),
    BIC(A4)
  ),

  LogLik = c(
    as.numeric(logLik(A1)),
    as.numeric(logLik(A2)),
    as.numeric(logLik(A3)),
    as.numeric(logLik(A4))
  ),

  Chisq = c(
    NA,
    model_comparisons$Chisq[2],
    model_comparisons$Chisq[3],
    model_comparisons$Chisq[4]
  ),

  Df = c(
    NA,
    model_comparisons$Df[2],
    model_comparisons$Df[3],
    model_comparisons$Df[4]
  ),

  p = c(
    NA,
    model_comparisons$`Pr(>Chisq)`[2],
    model_comparisons$`Pr(>Chisq)`[3],
    model_comparisons$`Pr(>Chisq)`[4]
  )
)

# Format values

attribute_model_table = attribute_model_table %>%
  mutate(
    AIC = sprintf(
      "%.1f",
      AIC
    ),

    BIC = sprintf(
      "%.1f",
      BIC
    ),

    LogLik = sprintf(
      "%.1f",
      LogLik
    ),

    Chisq = ifelse(
      is.na(Chisq),
      "",
      sprintf(
        "%.2f",
        Chisq
      )
    ),

    Df = ifelse(
      is.na(Df),
      "",
      as.character(Df)
    ),

    p = sapply(
      p,
      function(x) {
        if (is.na(x)) {
          ""
        } else {
          fmt_p(x)
        }
      }
    )
  )

# Print table

attribute_model_table %>%

  kable(
    caption =
      "Step-Up Model Comparisons for Researcher Attribute Ratings",

    col.names = c(
      "Model",
      "Predictors",
      "AIC",
      "BIC",
      "Log Likelihood",
      "χ²",
      "Δdf",
      "p"
    ),

    align = c(
      "l",
      "l",
      "r",
      "r",
      "r",
      "r",
      "r",
      "r"
    ),

    escape = FALSE
  ) %>%

  kable_styling(
    full_width = FALSE,
    font_size = 11,
    bootstrap_options =
      c(
        "condensed",
        "bordered"
      )
  ) %>%

  footnote(
    general =
      "Models were compared using likelihood-ratio tests. All models included random intercepts for participant and vignette. Attribute was sum coded. QRP Severity was effect coded as minor = −1, moderate = 0, and major = 1.",

    general_title =
```

```{r attribute_descriptives}

# Get the number and percentage of participants who chose
# each researcher for each attribute and vignette

attribute_descriptives = attr_model_dat %>%
  group_by(vignette_id, severity_num, attribute, researcher_ec) %>%
  summarise(
    N = sum(chosen == 1, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  group_by(vignette_id, severity_num, attribute) %>%
  mutate(
    Total_N = sum(N),
    Percent = round(N / Total_N * 100, 2)
  ) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(
    names_from = researcher_ec,
    values_from = c(N, Percent),
    values_fill = 0,
    names_glue = "{.value}_{researcher_ec}"
  ) %>%
  rename(
    Investigator_N = `N_-1`,
    Inspector_N = `N_1`,
    Investigator_Percent = `Percent_-1`,
    Inspector_Percent = `Percent_1`
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

print(attribute_descriptives, n = 27)
```

# Integrity & LIKEABILITY ANALYSIS (RQ1, RQ2) + TRUENESS (RQ3)

Research Question 1: How is integrity influenced by role and QRP
severity? • Hypothesis 1a: Inspectors will be rated higher in integrity
than investigators. • Hypothesis 1b: The relative integrity of
inspectors versus investigators will increase as QRP severity increases.

Research Question 2: How is likeability influenced by role and QRP
severity? • Hypothesis 2a: Investigators will be rated more likable than
inspectors. • Hypothesis 2b: At low QRP severity, investigators will be
rated as more likeable than inspectors, but at high QRP severity,
inspectors will be rated as more likeable than investigators.

Research Question 3: Is the perceived trueness of the finding influenced
by QRP severity? • Hypothesis 3: Perceived trueness will decrease as QRP
severity increases.

Research Questions 1–2: Integrity and Likeability Step-up MLMs will test
Role, Severity, and Role × Severity interaction:

Model 1: Integrity/Likeabilityijk = γ000 + γ100 (Researcherj) + ν0k +
μ0jk + εijk Model 2: Integrity/Likeabilityijk = γ000 + γ010
(Severityk) + ν0k + μ0k + εijk Model 3: Integrity/Likeabilityijk =
γ000 + γ100 (Researcherj) + γ010 (Severityk) + ν0k + μ0jk + εijk Model
4: Integrity/Likeabilityijk = γ000 + γ100 (Researcherj) + γ010
(Severityk) + γ110(Researcherj × Severityk) + ν0k + μ0jk + εijk

Research Question 3: Trueness of Findings Model FT1: Truenessijk= γ000 +
γ010 (Severityk) + ν0k + μ0j + εijk

## Build dataset

```{r build-Integrity-long}
# Vignette metadata
# Each vignette pair: investigator (inv) and inspector (insp)
# Severity:minor = vignette K/S, moderate = H/F, major = X/Y
# Integrity items: hon, sin, eth  (honest, sincere, ethical)
# Likeability: like, app (likeable, approachable)
# Trueness (conf): investigator only, 1 item per vignette

vignette_map = list(
  list(vig_letter = "k", vig_id = "minor",    role = "investigator",
       hon = "khon", sin = "ksin",  eth = "keth",
       like = "klike",  app = "kapp",  conf = "kcon"),
  list(vig_letter = "s", vig_id = "minor",    role = "inspector",
       hon = "shon",    sin = "ssin",  eth = "seth",
       like = "slike",  app = "sapp",  conf = NA),
  list(vig_letter = "h", vig_id = "moderate", role = "investigator",
       hon = "hhon",    sin = "hsin",  eth = "heth",
       like = "hlike",  app = "happ",  conf = "hcon"),
  list(vig_letter = "f", vig_id = "moderate", role = "inspector",
       hon = "fhon",    sin = "fsin",  eth = "feth",
       like = "flike",  app = "fapp",  conf = NA),
  list(vig_letter = "x", vig_id = "major",    role = "investigator",
       hon = "xhon",   sin = "xsin",  eth = "xeth",
       like = "xlike",  app = "xapp",  conf = "xcon"),
  list(vig_letter = "y", vig_id = "major",    role = "inspector",
       hon = "yhon",    sin = "ysin",  eth = "yeth",
       like = "ylike",  app = "yapp",  conf = NA)
)
# vig_letter is the TRUE vignette identifier (6 distinct narrative vignettes:
# k/s/h/f/x/y). vig_id (severity) is NOT a valid vignette-level random effect
# on its own — it only has 3 levels and is perfectly confounded with
# severity_num, the key fixed effect. vig_letter fixes this: it captures
# idiosyncratic vignette-writing variance independent of role and severity.

#Helper: extract numeric value from labelled string
parse_num = function(x) as.numeric(str_extract(as.character(x), "^\\d"))

#Build one row per participant × vignette × role
tl_rows = bind_rows(lapply(vignette_map, function(v) {
  filtered_by_age %>%                          # use cleaned dataset
    transmute(
      responseid,
      vig_letter = v$vig_letter,
      vig_id   = v$vig_id,
      role     = v$role,
      hon_raw  = parse_num(.data[[v$hon]]),
      sin_raw  = parse_num(.data[[v$sin]]),
      eth_raw  = parse_num(.data[[v$eth]]),
      like_raw = parse_num(.data[[v$like]]),
      app_raw  = parse_num(.data[[v$app]]),
      conf_raw = if (!is.na(v$conf)) parse_num(.data[[v$conf]]) else NA_real_
    )
}))

#Composites & factors
tl_dat = tl_rows %>%
  mutate(
    Integrity      = rowMeans(cbind(hon_raw, sin_raw, eth_raw), na.rm = TRUE),
    likeability = rowMeans(cbind(like_raw, app_raw), na.rm = TRUE),
    severity   = factor(vig_id,   levels = c("minor", "moderate", "major")),
    role       = factor(role,     levels = c("investigator", "inspector")),
    responseid = factor(responseid),
    vignette_id = factor(vig_letter, levels = c("k","s","h","f","x","y")),
    # effect-coded predictors
    role_ec    = if_else(role == "inspector", 1, -1),
    severity_num = case_when(
      severity == "minor" ~ 0,
      severity == "moderate" ~ 1,
      severity == "major" ~ 2
    )
  )

glimpse(tl_dat)
```

##Model-building strategy

The analyses below use the preregistered step-up structure for each
outcome. Models are fit using maximum likelihood (REML = FALSE) so that
fixed-effect models can be compared with likelihood-ratio tests. Random
slopes are evaluated first for the fully specified interaction model and
are stepped down only when the more complex structure is singular. The
resulting random-effects structure is then held constant across Models 0–4
so that the likelihood-ratio comparisons test changes in the fixed-effects
structure rather than changes in the random-effects structure.

### Model sequence for Integrity and Likeability

- Model 0: Null model
- Model 1: Role
- Model 2: QRP Severity
- Model 3: Role + QRP Severity
- Model 4: Role × QRP Severity

Model 1 tests the main effect of researcher role, corresponding to H1a for
Integrity and H2a for Likeability. Model 4 tests the Role × QRP Severity
interaction, corresponding to H1b and H2b.

```{r model-helpers}
library(lme4)
library(lmerTest)
library(emmeans)
library(knitr)
library(kableExtra)

# Extract fixed effects, including Satterthwaite df, t, and p.
get_fixed_effects = function(model) {
  cf = summary(model)$coefficients

  data.frame(
    Parameter = rownames(cf),
    b = cf[, "Estimate"],
    SE = cf[, "Std. Error"],
    df = cf[, "df"],
    t = cf[, "t value"],
    p = cf[, "Pr(>|t|)"],
    row.names = NULL,
    check.names = FALSE
  )
}

# APA-friendly p-value formatting.
fmt_p = function(p) {
  if (is.na(p)) return("")
  if (p < .001) return("< .001")
  formatC(p, digits = 3, format = "f")
}

# APA-friendly number formatting.
fmt_num = function(x, digits = 2) {
  if (length(x) == 0 || is.na(x)) return("")
  formatC(x, digits = digits, format = "f")
}

# Rename model terms for tables.
relabel_terms = function(x) {
  dplyr::recode(
    x,
    "(Intercept)" = "Intercept",
    "role_ec" = "Role",
    "severity_num" = "QRP Severity",
    "role_ec:severity_num" = "Role × QRP Severity",
    .default = x
  )
}

# Likelihood-ratio comparison of two nested ML models.
compare_models = function(previous, current) {
  lr = anova(previous, current)
  data.frame(
    Chisq = lr$Chisq[2],
    df = lr$Df[2],
    p = lr$`Pr(>Chisq)`[2]
  )
}

# Build a model-fit table. Each chi-square is the LR test against
# the immediately preceding model.
model_fit_table = function(models, names) {
  out = lapply(seq_along(models), function(i) {
    m = models[[i]]

    if (i == 1) {
      chisq = NA_real_
      df = NA_real_
      p = NA_real_
    } else {
      lr = compare_models(models[[i - 1]], m)
      chisq = lr$Chisq
      df = lr$df
      p = lr$p
    }

    data.frame(
      Model = names[i],
      AIC = AIC(m),
      BIC = BIC(m),
      logLik = as.numeric(logLik(m)),
      Chisq = chisq,
      df = df,
      p = p,
      check.names = FALSE
    )
  })

  dplyr::bind_rows(out) %>%
    mutate(
      AIC = round(AIC, 1),
      BIC = round(BIC, 1),
      logLik = round(logLik, 1),
      Chisq = ifelse(is.na(Chisq), "—", sprintf("%.2f", Chisq)),
      df = ifelse(is.na(df), "—", as.character(df)),
      p = ifelse(is.na(p), "—", vapply(p, fmt_p, character(1)))
    )
}

# Extract variance components.
get_variance_components = function(model) {
  vc = as.data.frame(VarCorr(model))
  vc %>%
    select(grp, vcov, sdcor) %>%
    mutate(
      Variance = round(vcov, 3),
      SD = round(sdcor, 3)
    ) %>%
    select(grp, Variance, SD)
}

# ICC for random-intercept components. Random slopes/covariances are not
# interpreted as simple ICC components here.
get_random_intercept_icc = function(model) {
  vc = as.data.frame(VarCorr(model))
  intercepts = vc %>%
    filter(is.na(var1) | var1 == "(Intercept)")

  residual = vc$vcov[vc$grp == "Residual"]
  total = sum(intercepts$vcov) + residual

  intercepts %>%
    mutate(ICC = round(vcov / total, 3)) %>%
    select(grp, ICC)
}
```

##Integrity

**Research Question 1: How is integrity influenced by role and QRP severity?**

**Hypothesis 1a:** Inspectors will be rated higher in integrity than
investigators.

**Hypothesis 1b:** The relative integrity of inspectors versus investigators
will increase as QRP severity increases.

###Random-effects structure for Integrity

```{r integrity-random-effects}

T4_max1 = lmer(
  Integrity ~ role_ec * severity_num +
    (1 + role_ec * severity_num | responseid),
  data = tl_dat,
  REML = FALSE,
  control = lmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa")
)

T4_max1_singular = isSingular(T4_max1, tol = 1e-4)
print(T4_max1_singular)

# Step down: remove random interaction slope

T4_max2 = lmer(
  Integrity ~ role_ec * severity_num +
    (1 + role_ec + severity_num | responseid),
  data = tl_dat,
  REML = FALSE,
  control = lmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa")
)

T4_max2_singular = isSingular(T4_max2, tol = 1e-4)
print(T4_max2_singular)


# Step down: retain random role slope only

T4_max3 = lmer(
  Integrity ~ role_ec * severity_num +
    (1 + role_ec | responseid),
  data = tl_dat,
  REML = FALSE,
  control = lmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa")
)

T4_max3_singular = isSingular(T4_max3, tol = 1e-4)
print(T4_max3_singular)

# Test preregistered vignette random intercept with the winning

T4_prereg = lmer(
  Integrity ~ role_ec * severity_num +
    (1 + role_ec | responseid) +
    (1 | vignette_id),
  data = tl_dat,
  REML = FALSE,
  control = lmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa")
)

T4_prereg_singular = isSingular(T4_prereg, tol = 1e-4)
print(T4_prereg_singular)


# Decision rule used throughout the analysis:
# retain the vignette intercept if the preregistered structure is
# non-singular; otherwise use the participant-only structure.
Integrity_uses_vignette_term = !T4_prereg_singular

cat(
  "Integrity final random-effects structure includes vignette intercept:",
  Integrity_uses_vignette_term,
  "\n"
)
```

###step-up models

```{r integrity-final-models}

if (Integrity_uses_vignette_term) {

  random_part_Integrity = "vignette"

  M0_Integrity = lmer(
    Integrity ~ 1 +
      (1 + role_ec | responseid) +
      (1 | vignette_id),
    data = tl_dat,
    REML = FALSE,
    control = lmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa")
  )

  T1 = lmer(
    Integrity ~ role_ec +
      (1 + role_ec | responseid) +
      (1 | vignette_id),
    data = tl_dat,
    REML = FALSE,
    control = lmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa")
  )

  T2 = lmer(
    Integrity ~ severity_num +
      (1 + role_ec | responseid) +
      (1 | vignette_id),
    data = tl_dat,
    REML = FALSE,
    control = lmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa")
  )

  T3 = lmer(
    Integrity ~ role_ec + severity_num +
      (1 + role_ec | responseid) +
      (1 | vignette_id),
    data = tl_dat,
    REML = FALSE,
    control = lmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa")
  )

  T4 = T4_prereg

} else {

  random_part_Integrity = "participant_only"

  M0_Integrity = lmer(
    Integrity ~ 1 +
      (1 + role_ec | responseid),
    data = tl_dat,
    REML = FALSE,
    control = lmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa")
  )

  T1 = lmer(
    Integrity ~ role_ec +
      (1 + role_ec | responseid),
    data = tl_dat,
    REML = FALSE,
    control = lmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa")
  )

  T2 = lmer(
    Integrity ~ severity_num +
      (1 + role_ec | responseid),
    data = tl_dat,
    REML = FALSE,
    control = lmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa")
  )

  T3 = lmer(
    Integrity ~ role_ec + severity_num +
      (1 + role_ec | responseid),
    data = tl_dat,
    REML = FALSE,
    control = lmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa")
  )

  T4 = T4_max3
}


# Singularity checks for final models.
cat("Integrity final model singularity:\n")
print(isSingular(M0_Integrity))
print(isSingular(T1))
print(isSingular(T2))
print(isSingular(T3))
print(isSingular(T4))


# Complete step-up comparison, including Model 0.
integrity_models = list(
  M0_Integrity,
  T1,
  T2,
  T3,
  T4
)

integrity_model_names = c(
  "Model 0: Null",
  "Model 1: Role",
  "Model 2: QRP Severity",
  "Model 3: Role + QRP Severity",
  "Model 4: Role × QRP Severity"
)

integrity_fit = model_fit_table(
  integrity_models,
  integrity_model_names
)

print(integrity_fit)


# Full model summaries.
summary(T1)
summary(T2)
summary(T3)
summary(T4)
```

###fixed effects and planned role contrasts

```{r integrity-results}
# Fixed effects from every model, including Satterthwaite df, t, and p.
integrity_fixed_effects = lapply(
  integrity_models,
  get_fixed_effects
)

names(integrity_fixed_effects) = paste0("Model_", 0:4)

print(integrity_fixed_effects)


# Planned comparison: inspectors versus investigators at each severity.
# Bonferroni correction is applied across the three severity-specific
# role comparisons.
emm_Integrity = emmeans(
  T4,
  ~ role_ec | severity_num,
  at = list(severity_num = c(0,1,2))
)

emm_Integrity_role = emmeans(
  T4,
  pairwise ~ role_ec | severity_num,
  at = list(severity_num = c(0,1,2)),
  adjust = "bonferroni"
)

summary(emm_Integrity_role$contrasts)


# Cohen's d for each role contrast.
eff_size(
  emm_Integrity,
  sigma = sigma(T4),
  edf = df.residual(T4)
)
```

##TRUENESS

Research Question 3: Is the perceived trueness of the finding influenced by
QRP severity?**

**Hypothesis 3:** Perceived trueness will decrease as QRP severity increases.

###data and model

```{r trueness-data}
# Trueness is only rated for investigators, with one item per vignette.
trueness_dat = filtered_by_age %>%
  transmute(
    responseid,
    minor = parse_num(kcon),
    moderate = parse_num(hcon),
    major = parse_num(xcon)
  ) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(minor, moderate, major),
    names_to = "severity",
    values_to = "trueness"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    severity = factor(
      severity,
      levels = c("minor", "moderate", "major")
    ),
    severity_num = case_when(
      severity == "minor" ~ 0,
      severity == "moderate" ~ 1,
      severity == "major" ~ 2
    ),
    responseid = factor(responseid),
    trueness_c = trueness - 3
  )


# Descriptives.
trueness_descriptives = trueness_dat %>%
  group_by(severity) %>%
  summarise(
    n = sum(!is.na(trueness)),
    M = round(mean(trueness, na.rm = TRUE), 2),
    SD = round(sd(trueness, na.rm = TRUE), 2),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

print(trueness_descriptives)
```

```{r trueness-model}
  trueness_c ~ severity_num +
    (1 | responseid) +

)

  at = list(severity_num = c(0,1,2)),

)

summary(emm_trueness$contrasts)

    ~ severity_num,
    at = list(severity_num = c(0,1,2))
  ),

)
```

```{r}
#APA Model Comparison Tables

# Helper: extract fixed effects from a model into a clean data frame
fe_table = function(model) {
  cf = summary(model)$coefficients
  ci = confint(model, method = "Wald")
  ci = ci[rownames(cf), ]

  data.frame(
    Parameter = rownames(cf),
    b         = round(cf[, "Estimate"], 2),
    SE        = round(cf[, "Std. Error"], 2),
    df        = round(cf[, "df"], 2),
    CI_low    = round(ci[, 1], 2),
    CI_high   = round(ci[, 2], 2),
    t         = round(cf[, "t value"], 2),
    p         = ifelse(
      cf[, "Pr(>|t|)"] < .001,
      "< .001",
      formatC(cf[, "Pr(>|t|)"], digits = 3, format = "f")
    )
  )
}


relabel = function(df) {
  df$Parameter = dplyr::recode(
    df$Parameter,
    "(Intercept)"          = "Intercept",
    "role_ec"              = "Role",
    "severity_num"         = "QRP Severity",
    "role_ec:severity_num" = "Role × QRP Severity"
  )
  df
}


fit_table = function(model_list, model_names) {

  do.call(
    rbind,
    lapply(seq_along(model_list), function(i) {

      m = model_list[[i]]

      if (i == 1) {

        chisq_out = NA_character_
        df_out    = NA_character_
        p_out     = NA_character_

      } else {

        lr = anova(
          model_list[[i - 1]],
          m
        )

        chisq_out = formatC(
          lr$Chisq[2],
          digits = 2,
          format = "f"
        )

        df_out = as.character(
          lr$Df[2]
        )

        p_out = ifelse(
          lr$`Pr(>Chisq)`[2] < .001,
          "< .001",
          formatC(
            lr$`Pr(>Chisq)`[2],
            digits = 3,
            format = "f"
          )
        )
      }

      data.frame(
        Model  = model_names[i],
        AIC    = round(AIC(m), 1),
        BIC    = round(BIC(m), 1),
        logLik = round(as.numeric(logLik(m)), 1),
        Chisq  = chisq_out,
        df     = df_out,
        p      = p_out
      )
    })
  )
}
```

```{r apa step up models}

get_fe = function(model) {

  cf = summary(model)$coefficients

  list(
    b  = setNames(
      round(cf[, "Estimate"], 2),
      rownames(cf)
    ),

    se = setNames(
      round(cf[, "Std. Error"], 2),
      rownames(cf)
    ),

    df = if ("df" %in% colnames(cf)) {
      setNames(
        round(cf[, "df"], 2),
        rownames(cf)
      )
    } else {
      NULL
    },

    t = if ("t value" %in% colnames(cf)) {
      setNames(
        round(cf[, "t value"], 2),
        rownames(cf)
      )
    } else {
      NULL
    },

    p = setNames(
      cf[, "Pr(>|t|)"],
      rownames(cf)
    )
  )
}

#format p value

fmt_p = function(p) {

  if (is.na(p)) return("")

  if (p < .001) {
    return("< .001***")
  }

  stars =
    ifelse(
      p < .01, "**",
      ifelse(
        p < .05, "*",
        ""
      )
    )

  paste0(
    formatC(
      p,
      digits = 3,
      format = "f"
    ),
    stars
  )
}


#extract one fixed effect 

cell = function(fe, term) {

  if (!term %in% names(fe$b)) {
    return(
      c("", "", "")
    )
  }

  c(
    as.character(fe$b[term]),
    as.character(fe$se[term]),
    fmt_p(fe$p[term])
  )
}

#Random effects

get_re = function(model) {

  vc = as.data.frame(
    lme4::VarCorr(model)
  )

  setNames(
    round(vc$vcov, 3),
    vc$grp
  )
}


#ICC

get_icc = function(model) {

  vc = as.data.frame(
    lme4::VarCorr(model)
  )

  total = sum(vc$vcov)

  setNames(
    round(
      vc$vcov / total,
      3
    ),
    vc$grp
  )
}

#table set up 

make_stepup_table = function(
    m0,
    m1,
    m2,
    m3,
    m4,
    caption_text,
    footnote_text
) {

  models = list(
    m0,
    m1,
    m2,
    m3,
    m4
  )

  fe_list = lapply(
    models,
    get_fe
  )

  re_list = lapply(
    models,
    get_re
  )

  icc_list = lapply(
    models,
    get_icc
  )

#fixed effect 

  term_labels = c(
    "(Intercept)" =
      "Intercept",

    "role_ec" =
      "Role",

    "severity_num" =
      "QRP Severity",

    "role_ec:severity_num" =
      "Role × QRP Severity"
  )


  rows = lapply(
    names(term_labels),
    function(term) {

      cells =
        do.call(
          cbind,
          lapply(
            fe_list,
            function(fe) cell(fe, term)
          )
        )


      data.frame(

        Parameter =
          term_labels[term],

        M0_b =
          cells[1, 1],

        M0_se =
          cells[2, 1],

        M0_p =
          cells[3, 1],


        M1_b =
          cells[1, 2],

        M1_se =
          cells[2, 2],

        M1_p =
          cells[3, 2],


        M2_b =
          cells[1, 3],

        M2_se =
          cells[2, 3],

        M2_p =
          cells[3, 3],


        M3_b =
          cells[1, 4],

        M3_se =
          cells[2, 4],

        M3_p =
          cells[3, 4],


        M4_b =
          cells[1, 5],

        M4_se =
          cells[2, 5],

        M4_p =
          cells[3, 5],

        stringsAsFactors = FALSE
      )
    }
  )


  fe_df =
    do.call(
      rbind,
      rows
    )


#random effects

  re_grps = c(

    "responseid" =
      "Participant variance",

    "vignette_id" =
      "Vignette variance",

    "Residual" =
      "Residual variance"
  )


  re_rows =
    lapply(
      names(re_grps),
      function(grp) {

        vals =
          sapply(
            re_list,
            function(re) {

              if (grp %in% names(re)) {

                as.character(
                  re[grp]
                )

              } else {

                "—"
              }
            }
          )


        data.frame(

          Parameter =
            re_grps[grp],

          M0_b = vals[1],
          M0_se = "",
          M0_p = "",

          M1_b = vals[2],
          M1_se = "",
          M1_p = "",

          M2_b = vals[3],
          M2_se = "",
          M2_p = "",

          M3_b = vals[4],
          M3_se = "",
          M3_p = "",

          M4_b = vals[5],
          M4_se = "",
          M4_p = "",

          stringsAsFactors = FALSE
        )
      }
    )


  re_df =
    do.call(
      rbind,
      re_rows
    )


#ICC

  icc_rows =
    lapply(
      c(
        "responseid",
        "vignette_id"
      ),
      function(grp) {

        vals =
          sapply(
            icc_list,
            function(ic) {

              if (grp %in% names(ic)) {

                as.character(
                  ic[grp]
                )

              } else {

                "—"
              }
            }
          )


        label =
          ifelse(
            grp == "responseid",
            "ICC: Participant",
            "ICC: Vignette"
          )


        data.frame(

          Parameter = label,

          M0_b = vals[1],
          M0_se = "",
          M0_p = "",

          M1_b = vals[2],
          M1_se = "",
          M1_p = "",

          M2_b = vals[3],
          M2_se = "",
          M2_p = "",

          M3_b = vals[4],
          M3_se = "",
          M3_p = "",

          M4_b = vals[5],
          M4_se = "",
          M4_p = "",

          stringsAsFactors = FALSE
        )
      }
    )


  icc_df =
    do.call(
      rbind,
      icc_rows
    )


# AIC and BIC
  fit_vals =
    sapply(
      models,
      function(m) {

        c(
          AIC = round(
            AIC(m),
            1
          ),

          BIC = round(
            BIC(m),
            1
          )
        )
      }
    )


  fit_df =
    data.frame(

      Parameter =
        c(
          "AIC",
          "BIC"
        ),

      M0_b =
        as.character(
          fit_vals[, 1]
        ),

      M0_se = "",
      M0_p = "",

      M1_b =
        as.character(
          fit_vals[, 2]
        ),

      M1_se = "",
      M1_p = "",

      M2_b =
        as.character(
          fit_vals[, 3]
        ),

      M2_se = "",
      M2_p = "",

      M3_b =
        as.character(
          fit_vals[, 4]
        ),

      M3_se = "",
      M3_p = "",

      M4_b =
        as.character(
          fit_vals[, 5]
        ),

      M4_se = "",
      M4_p = "",

      stringsAsFactors = FALSE
    )
  
#model comparison

  comparisons = list()

  for (i in 2:5) {

    comp =
      anova(
        models[[i - 1]],
        models[[i]]
      )

    chi =
      comp$Chisq[2]

    df =
      comp$Df[2]

    p =
      comp$`Pr(>Chisq)`[2]


    comparisons[[i - 1]] =
      c(
        chi,
        df,
        p
      )
  }


  comparison_df =
    data.frame(

      Parameter =
        c(
          "Model comparison χ²",
          "Model comparison df",
          "Model comparison p"
        ),

      M0_b = "—",
      M0_se = "",
      M0_p = "",

      M1_b =
        as.character(
          round(
            comparisons[[1]][1],
            2
          )
        ),

      M1_se =
        as.character(
          comparisons[[1]][2]
        ),

      M1_p =
        fmt_p(
          comparisons[[1]][3]
        ),


      M2_b =
        as.character(
          round(
            comparisons[[2]][1],
            2
          )
        ),

      M2_se =
        as.character(
          comparisons[[2]][2]
        ),

      M2_p =
        fmt_p(
          comparisons[[2]][3]
        ),


      M3_b =
        as.character(
          round(
            comparisons[[3]][1],
            2
          )
        ),

      M3_se =
        as.character(
          comparisons[[3]][2]
        ),

      M3_p =
        fmt_p(
          comparisons[[3]][3]
        ),


      M4_b =
        as.character(
          round(
            comparisons[[4]][1],
            2
          )
        ),

      M4_se =
        as.character(
          comparisons[[4]][2]
        ),

      M4_p =
        fmt_p(
          comparisons[[4]][3]
        ),

      stringsAsFactors = FALSE
    )


  full_df =
    rbind(
      fe_df,
      re_df,
      icc_df,
      fit_df,
      comparison_df
    )


  full_df %>%

    kable(

      caption =
        caption_text,

      col.names =
        c(
          "Parameter",

          "b", "SE", "p",
          "b", "SE", "p",
          "b", "SE", "p",
          "b", "SE", "p",
          "b", "SE", "p"
        ),

      align =
        c(
          "l",
          rep(
            "r",
            15
          )
        ),

      escape = FALSE
    ) %>%

    kable_styling(

      full_width = TRUE,

      font_size = 11,

      bootstrap_options =
        c(
          "condensed",
          "bordered"
        )
    ) %>%

add_header_above(
  c(
    " " = 2,
    "Model 0" = 3,
    "Model 1" = 3,
    "Model 2" = 3,
    "Model 3" = 3,
    "Model 4" = 3
  )
    ) %>%

    footnote(

      general =
        footnote_text,

      general_title =
        "Note.",

      footnote_as_chunk =
        TRUE
    )
}
```

```{r INTEGRITY TABLE}
    "Role was effect coded as inspector = 1 and investigator = −1. QRP Severity: minor = 0, moderate = 1, major = 2. Model comparison χ² values are likelihood-ratio tests comparing each model with the preceding model. * p < .05. ** p < .01. *** p < .001."
)
```

```{r trueness-table}
# Fixed effects
ft1 <- summary(FT1)$coefficients

# Random effects
ft1_vc <- as.data.frame(
  lme4::VarCorr(FT1)
)

# Extract variance components
participant_var <- ft1_vc$vcov[
  ft1_vc$grp == "responseid"
]

vignette_var <- ft1_vc$vcov[
  ft1_vc$grp == "severity"
]

residual_var <- ft1_vc$vcov[
  ft1_vc$grp == "Residual"
]

# Total variance
total_var <-
  participant_var +
  vignette_var +
  residual_var

# ICCs
participant_icc <-
  participant_var / total_var

vignette_icc <-
  vignette_var / total_var


# Create table

trueness_df <- data.frame(

  Parameter = c(
    "Intercept",
    "QRP Severity",
    "Participant variance",
```

```{r}
# Model A0

A0 = glmer(
  chosen ~ attribute +
    (1 | responseid) +
    (1 | vignette_id),
  data = attr_model_dat,
  family = binomial,
  control = glmerControl(
    optimizer = "bobyqa",
    optCtrl = list(maxfun = 2e5)
  )
)


# Fixed effects

a0 <- summary(A0)$coefficients
a1 <- summary(A1)$coefficients
a2 <- summary(A2)$coefficients
a3 <- summary(A3)$coefficients
a4 <- summary(A4)$coefficients


# Random effects

a0_vc <- as.data.frame(lme4::VarCorr(A0))
a1_vc <- as.data.frame(lme4::VarCorr(A1))
a2_vc <- as.data.frame(lme4::VarCorr(A2))
a3_vc <- as.data.frame(lme4::VarCorr(A3))
a4_vc <- as.data.frame(lme4::VarCorr(A4))


# Extract variance components

a0_participant_var <- a0_vc$vcov[a0_vc$grp == "responseid"]
a1_participant_var <- a1_vc$vcov[a1_vc$grp == "responseid"]
a2_participant_var <- a2_vc$vcov[a2_vc$grp == "responseid"]
a3_participant_var <- a3_vc$vcov[a3_vc$grp == "responseid"]
a4_participant_var <- a4_vc$vcov[a4_vc$grp == "responseid"]

a0_vignette_var <- a0_vc$vcov[a0_vc$grp == "vignette_id"]
a1_vignette_var <- a1_vc$vcov[a1_vc$grp == "vignette_id"]
a2_vignette_var <- a2_vc$vcov[a2_vc$grp == "vignette_id"]
a3_vignette_var <- a3_vc$vcov[a3_vc$grp == "vignette_id"]
a4_vignette_var <- a4_vc$vcov[a4_vc$grp == "vignette_id"]


# Residual variance for logistic models

residual_var <- pi^2 / 3


# Total variance

a0_total_var <- a0_participant_var + a0_vignette_var + residual_var
a1_total_var <- a1_participant_var + a1_vignette_var + residual_var
a2_total_var <- a2_participant_var + a2_vignette_var + residual_var
a3_total_var <- a3_participant_var + a3_vignette_var + residual_var
a4_total_var <- a4_participant_var + a4_vignette_var + residual_var


# ICCs

a1_participant_icc <- a1_participant_var / a1_total_var
a2_participant_icc <- a2_participant_var / a2_total_var
a3_participant_icc <- a3_participant_var / a3_total_var

a1_vignette_icc <- a1_vignette_var / a1_total_var
a2_vignette_icc <- a2_vignette_var / a2_total_var
a3_vignette_icc <- a3_vignette_var / a3_total_var
a4_vignette_icc <- a4_vignette_var / a4_total_var


# Create table
```

#EFA

```{r EFA}
# Load packages
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(lavaan)
library(semTools)

# 1. Create participant-level data


cfa_dat <- tl_dat %>%
  group_by(responseid, role) %>%
  summarise(
    hon  = mean(hon_raw,  na.rm = TRUE),
    sin  = mean(sin_raw,  na.rm = TRUE),
    eth  = mean(eth_raw,  na.rm = TRUE),
    like = mean(like_raw, na.rm = TRUE),
    app  = mean(app_raw,  na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )


# 2. One-factor model

one_factor <- '
  Evaluation =~ hon + sin + eth + like + app
'


# Investigator: one-factor model
investigator_one <- cfa(
  one_factor,
  data = cfa_dat %>% filter(role == "investigator"),
  missing = "fiml"
)

# Inspector: one-factor model
inspector_one <- cfa(
  one_factor,
  data = cfa_dat %>% filter(role == "inspector"),
  missing = "fiml"
)


# 3. Two-factor model

two_factor <- '
  Integrity =~ hon + sin + eth
  Likeability =~ like + app
'


# Investigator: two-factor model
investigator_two <- cfa(
  two_factor,
  data = cfa_dat %>% filter(role == "investigator"),
  missing = "fiml"
)

# Inspector: two-factor model
inspector_two <- cfa(
  two_factor,
  data = cfa_dat %>% filter(role == "inspector"),
  missing = "fiml"
)


# 4. Print model results


cat("\n================ INVESTIGATOR: ONE FACTOR ================\n")
summary(
  investigator_one,
  fit.measures = TRUE,
  standardized = TRUE
)

cat("\n================ INVESTIGATOR: TWO FACTORS ================\n")
summary(
  investigator_two,
  fit.measures = TRUE,
  standardized = TRUE
)

cat("\n================ INSPECTOR: ONE FACTOR ================\n")
summary(
  inspector_one,
  fit.measures = TRUE,
  standardized = TRUE
)

cat("\n================ INSPECTOR: TWO FACTORS ================\n")
summary(
  inspector_two,
  fit.measures = TRUE,
  standardized = TRUE
)

# 5. Compare one-factor vs. two-factor models


cat("\n================ MODEL COMPARISONS ================\n")

cat("\nInvestigator:\n")
anova(
  investigator_one,
  investigator_two
)

cat("\nInspector:\n")
anova(
  inspector_one,
  inspector_two
)


# 6. Create easy-to-read fit table


fit_table <- rbind(
  Investigator_1Factor = fitMeasures(
    investigator_one,
    c("chisq", "df", "cfi", "tli", "rmsea", "srmr")
  ),
  
  Investigator_2Factor = fitMeasures(
    investigator_two,
    c("chisq", "df", "cfi", "tli", "rmsea", "srmr")
  ),
  
  Inspector_1Factor = fitMeasures(
    inspector_one,
    c("chisq", "df", "cfi", "tli", "rmsea", "srmr")
  ),
  
  Inspector_2Factor = fitMeasures(
    inspector_two,
    c("chisq", "df", "cfi", "tli", "rmsea", "srmr")
  )
)

cat("\n================ FIT TABLE ================\n")
print(round(fit_table, 3))


# 7. Measurement invariance across researcher role

# ONLY run/interpret this section if the two-factor model
# provides a reasonable fit.
#
# Configural = same factor structure
# Metric     = equal factor loadings
# Scalar     = equal loadings + intercepts


cat("\n================ CONFIGURAL INVARIANCE ================\n")

configural <- cfa(
  two_factor,
  data = cfa_dat,
  group = "role",
  missing = "fiml"
)

summary(
  configural,
  fit.measures = TRUE,
  standardized = TRUE
)


cat("\n================ METRIC INVARIANCE ================\n")

metric <- cfa(
  two_factor,
  data = cfa_dat,
  group = "role",
  group.equal = "loadings",
  missing = "fiml"
)

summary(
  metric,
  fit.measures = TRUE,
  standardized = TRUE
)


cat("\n================ SCALAR INVARIANCE ================\n")

scalar <- cfa(
  two_factor,
  data = cfa_dat,
  group = "role",
  group.equal = c("loadings", "intercepts"),
  missing = "fiml"
)

summary(
  scalar,
  fit.measures = TRUE,
  standardized = TRUE
)

# 8. Compare invariance models

cat("\n================ INVARIANCE MODEL COMPARISON ================\n")

anova(
  configural,
  metric,
  scalar
)

# 9. Invariance fit table

invariance_fit_table <- rbind(
  Configural = fitMeasures(
    configural,
    c("chisq", "df", "cfi", "tli", "rmsea", "srmr")
  ),
  
  Metric = fitMeasures(
    metric,
    c("chisq", "df", "cfi", "tli", "rmsea", "srmr")
  ),
  
  Scalar = fitMeasures(
    scalar,
    c("chisq", "df", "cfi", "tli", "rmsea", "srmr")
  )
)

cat("\n================ INVARIANCE FIT TABLE ================\n")
print(round(invariance_fit_table, 3))
```
```{r}

# 10. Create publication-ready measurement invariance table


library(knitr)
library(kableExtra)

# Extract fit statistics
invariance_table <- data.frame(
  Model = c("Configural", "Metric", "Scalar"),
  
  Chi_Square = c(
    fitMeasures(configural, "chisq"),
    fitMeasures(metric, "chisq"),
    fitMeasures(scalar, "chisq")
  ),
  
  df = c(
    fitMeasures(configural, "df"),
    fitMeasures(metric, "df"),
    fitMeasures(scalar, "df")
  ),
  
  CFI = c(
    fitMeasures(configural, "cfi"),
    fitMeasures(metric, "cfi"),
    fitMeasures(scalar, "cfi")
  ),
  
  TLI = c(
    fitMeasures(configural, "tli"),
    fitMeasures(metric, "tli"),
    fitMeasures(scalar, "tli")
  ),
  
  RMSEA = c(
    fitMeasures(configural, "rmsea"),
    fitMeasures(metric, "rmsea"),
    fitMeasures(scalar, "rmsea")
  ),
  
  SRMR = c(
    fitMeasures(configural, "srmr"),
    fitMeasures(metric, "srmr"),
    fitMeasures(scalar, "srmr")
  )
)

# Add change in fit indices
invariance_table$Delta_CFI <- c(
  NA,
  invariance_table$CFI[2] - invariance_table$CFI[1],
  invariance_table$CFI[3] - invariance_table$CFI[2]
)

invariance_table$Delta_RMSEA <- c(
  NA,
  invariance_table$RMSEA[2] - invariance_table$RMSEA[1],
  invariance_table$RMSEA[3] - invariance_table$RMSEA[2]
)

# Round values
invariance_table <- invariance_table %>%
  mutate(
    Chi_Square = round(Chi_Square, 2),
    CFI = round(CFI, 3),
    TLI = round(TLI, 3),
    RMSEA = round(RMSEA, 3),
    SRMR = round(SRMR, 3),
    Delta_CFI = round(Delta_CFI, 3),
    Delta_RMSEA = round(Delta_RMSEA, 3)
  )

# Display table
kable(
  invariance_table,
  format = "html",
  caption = "Measurement Invariance Across Researcher Role"
) %>%
  kable_styling(
    bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"),
    full_width = FALSE
)
```
```{r}

# FIGURE: One-Factor vs. Two-Factor Model Fit
# Investigator vs. Inspector


library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)

# Create model comparison data
model_comparison <- data.frame(
  Role = rep(c("Investigator", "Inspector"), each = 2),
  Model = rep(c("One Factor", "Two Factors"), 2),

  CFI = c(
    fitMeasures(investigator_one, "cfi"),
    fitMeasures(investigator_two, "cfi"),
    fitMeasures(inspector_one, "cfi"),
    fitMeasures(inspector_two, "cfi")
  ),

  RMSEA = c(
    fitMeasures(investigator_one, "rmsea"),
    fitMeasures(investigator_two, "rmsea"),
    fitMeasures(inspector_one, "rmsea"),
    fitMeasures(inspector_two, "rmsea")
  )
)

# Set order
model_comparison$Model <- factor(
  model_comparison$Model,
  levels = c("One Factor", "Two Factors")
)

# Convert to long format
plot_data <- model_comparison %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(CFI, RMSEA),
    names_to = "Fit_Index",
    values_to = "Value"
  )

# Plot

ggplot(
  plot_data,
  aes(
    x = Model,
    y = Value,
    group = Role,
    color = Role
  )
) +

  # Lines
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.2) +

  # Points
  geom_point(size = 4) +

  # Value labels
  geom_text(
    aes(
      label = sprintf("%.3f", Value),
      vjust = ifelse(
        Model == "One Factor",
        1.7,
        -1.2
      )
    ),
    size = 4,
    fontface = "bold",
    show.legend = FALSE
  ) +

  # Separate panels for CFI and RMSEA
  facet_wrap(
    ~ Fit_Index,
    scales = "free_y"
  ) +

  # Labels
  labs(
    title = "Two-Factor Model Provides Better Fit",
    subtitle = "Model fit for Investigator and Inspector ratings",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Fit Index",
    color = "Researcher Role"
  ) +

  # Colors
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c(
      "Investigator" = "#2166AC",
      "Inspector" = "#D73027"
    )
  ) +

  # Theme
  theme_classic(base_size = 14) +

  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(
      face = "bold",
      size = 18
    ),

    plot.subtitle = element_text(
      size = 13
    ),

    strip.text = element_text(
      face = "bold",
      size = 14
    ),

    legend.position = "bottom",

    legend.title = element_text(
      face = "bold"
    ),

      size = 12
    )
  )
```

#exploratory anovas

#INTEGRITYANOVA
```{r}
#Exploratory ANOVAs: Severity as categorical

# INTEGRITY ANOVA
# Role = within-subjects
# Severity = within-subjects

integrity_anova_dat = tl_dat %>%
  mutate(
    Role = factor(
      role,
      levels = c("investigator", "inspector"),
      labels = c("Investigator", "Inspector")
    ),
    Severity = factor(
      severity_num,
      levels = c(0, 1, 2),
      labels = c("Minor", "Moderate", "Major")
    ),
    Participant = factor(responseid)
  )

integrity_rm_anova = aov_ez(
  id = "Participant",
  dv = "Integrity",
  data = integrity_anova_dat,
  within = c("Role", "Severity"),
  type = 3,
  fun_aggregate = mean
)

integrity_rm_anova
```


#LIKEABILITYANOVA
```{r}
# LIKEABILITY ANOVA
# Role = within-subjects
# Severity = within-subjects


like_anova_dat <- model.frame(L4) %>%
  mutate(
    Role = factor(
      role_ec,
      levels = c(-1, 1),
      labels = c("Investigator", "Inspector")
    ),
    Severity = factor(
      severity_num,
      levels = c(0, 1, 2),
      labels = c("Minor", "Moderate", "Major")
    ),
    Participant = factor(responseid)
  )

like_rm_anova <- aov_ez(
  id = "Participant",
  dv = "likeability",
  data = like_anova_dat,
  within = c("Role", "Severity"),
  type = 3,
  fun_aggregate = mean
)

like_rm_anova
```
